title: Ratchet cross-owner enforcement invariants

intent.outcome: Satisfy #2762 by extending the existing context-authority registry and #2300 composed-operation release gate so one admitted revision-bound operating decision remains the sole ordinary authority for owner, action, permission, proof/claim, and continuation across source, installed, generated, and adapter consumers.
non_goals: Do not create a new authority registry, constraint language, workflow command, or durable decision ledger.
Do not move specialist facts out of Planning, Verification, Memory, config, target identity, evaluation, or external-intent owners.
Do not promote provider-specific review or packed-artifact behavior into the generic kernel.
Do not weaken fail-closed admission, construct Planning custody for quiet direct work, or treat cost reduction as correctness authority.

parent.contribution: Turns the merged dogfooding counterexamples into release-gating invariants required by parent #2562 before non-local delegation is exercised.
parent.closure_boundary: This slice may close only #2762; #2562, #2721, #2763, and the all-open-issues decomposition remain live.

owned: generated workspace contract resources and conformance receipts derived from these canonical sources
release changeset and Planning integration evidence for #2762
effects: The canonical registry names one join identity and one disposition for every decision-relevant fact and peer representation covered by the ordinary loop.
Operating decisions expose a mechanically derived cross-owner enforcement projection bound to their canonical decision identity.
The composed-operation release gate rejects stale or conflicting identity, prerequisite, permission, proof-publication, bounded-custody, residue, and peer-surface counterexamples.
Generated and installed consumers carry the same registry-derived invariant contract without acquiring semantic authority.

refs: 25 dogfooding counterexample and safe-control tests passed
workspace lint, typecheck, contract tooling, and generated package checks passed

delegation.reason: No sub-agent delegation was requested; this release-gate layer is a bounded continuation of the exact stacked head.

next_action: Commit the validated enforcement ratchet, open the third stacked PR on PR #2776 exact head, and observe hosted checks without claiming review authority.

claims: One admitted input snapshot cannot yield divergent authoritative owner, action, permission, proof/claim, or continuation answers.
Deterministic prerequisites and binding mismatches fail before execution or mutation with one typed executable recovery.
Evidence publication is fixed-point safe unless a declared semantic dependency changes; bounded effects and future residue retain correct custody.
New first-line peer decision authority fails the release gate unless an existing surface is removed, demoted, or mechanically derived.
requirements: Run focused registry, operating-decision, composed-scenario, proof, bounded-effect, and residue fixtures including weak-agent negatives and safe counterexamples.
Run contract tooling, generated package parity, installed consumer readiness, operation conformance, lint, typecheck, and workspace-wide checks.
Publish a stacked PR based on PR #2776 exact head; hosted checks and independent review remain external authority.

continuation.residual_intent: After this lane, implement #2763 and then reconcile parent closure.

execution_bounds.branch_order: codex/open-issues-enforcement-ratchet bases on codex/open-issues-verifier-authority exact head.
execution_bounds.ask_before: Adding a new root command, authority store, policy language, or weakening a canonical source-owner boundary.
execution_bounds.stop_conditions: Stop if an invariant cannot be derived from the existing registry and operating decision, or if a child defect is not already fixed at its canonical source.
